\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Granger precedence is not causation.}
Our claim is scoped to temporal predictive improvement~\cite{granger1969investigating,shojaie2022granger}; bivariate tests cannot exclude confounders, and the entropy$\to$diversity ordering may partly reflect differential metric sensitivity rather than a strict process-level cascade.
The detection boundary $\alpha_c(T{=}10) \approx 0.49$ (bootstrap 95\% CI: $[0.43, 0.56]$) is contingent on method, $T$, and metric choice; Proposition~\ref{prop:phase-boundary} derives it from a sub-linear signal model ($R^2{=}0.883$), with predict-then-verify at $T{=}20$ revealing systematic conservative bias at boundary $\alpha$ consistent with $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling.
The synchronous dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ persists across tested $T{\geq}10$ ($T{=}10$, $15$, $20$; $p{=}0.064$ at $T{=}20$), suggesting a structural regime distinct from the CMR of \citet{gu2024cmr}.
The detectability landscape is far more structured than previously assumed: blind zones, sharp onsets, synchronous dips, and method-dependent terrain.
PermG identifies token entropy as a one-generation-ahead canary, tested across 15 model-seed combinations (five families, 345M--6.9B) with unambiguous forward detection in 10 and cascade ordering in 14 (\S\ref{sec:generalization}); canary-based cessation reduces peak perplexity by 58\% (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}).

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Granger precedence is not causation.}
Our claim is scoped to temporal predictive improvement~\cite{granger1969investigating,shojaie2022granger}; bivariate tests cannot exclude confounders, and the entropy$\to$diversity ordering may partly reflect differential metric sensitivity rather than a strict process-level cascade.
The detection boundary $\alpha_c(T{=}10) \approx 0.49$ (bootstrap 95\% CI: $[0.43, 0.56]$) is contingent on method, $T$, and metric choice; Proposition~\ref{prop:phase-boundary} derives it from a sub-linear signal model ($R^2{=}0.883$), with predict-then-verify at $T{=}20$ revealing systematic conservative bias at boundary $\alpha$ consistent with $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling.
The synchronous dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ persists across tested $T{\geq}10$ ($T{=}10$, $15$, $20$; $p{=}0.064$ at $T{=}20$), suggesting a structural regime distinct from the CMR of \citet{gu2024cmr}.
The detectability landscape is far more structured than previously assumed: blind zones, sharp onsets, synchronous dips, and method-dependent terrain.
PermG identifies token entropy as a one-generation-ahead canary, tested across 15 model-seed combinations (five families, 345M--6.9B) with unambiguous forward detection in 10 and cascade ordering in 14 (\S\ref{sec:generalization}); canary-based cessation reduces peak perplexity by 58\% (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}).

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Granger precedence is not causation.}
Our claim is scoped to temporal predictive improvement~\cite{granger1969investigating,shojaie2022granger}; bivariate tests cannot exclude confounders, and the entropy$\to$diversity ordering may partly reflect differential metric sensitivity rather than a strict process-level cascade.
The detection boundary $\alpha_c(T{=}10) \approx 0.49$ (bootstrap 95\% CI: $[0.43, 0.56]$) is contingent on method, $T$, and metric choice; Proposition~\ref{prop:phase-boundary} derives it from a sub-linear signal model ($R^2{=}0.883$); predict-then-verify at $T{=}20$ reveals systematic conservative bias at boundary $\alpha$.
The synchronous dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ persists across $T{=}10$, $15$, $20$ ($p{=}0.064$ at $T{=}20$), suggesting a structural regime distinct from the CMR of \citet{gu2024cmr}.
The detectability landscape---blind zones, sharp onsets, synchronous dips, method-dependent terrain---is far more structured than previously assumed.
PermG identifies token entropy as a one-generation-ahead canary (forward detection in 10/15, cascade in 14/15 conditions across five families, 345M--6.9B; \S\ref{sec:generalization}); canary-based cessation reduces peak perplexity by 58\% (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_discussion}).

PermG identifies entropy as a one-generation-ahead canary (detection in 10/15, cascade in 14/15 across five families; \S\ref{sec:generalization}); canary-based cessation reduces peak perplexity by 58\%.

lines: \paragraph{Granger precedence is not causation.}

Our claim is scoped to temporal predictive improvement~\cite{granger1969investigating,shojaie2022granger}; bivariate tests cannot exclude confounders, and the entropy$\to$diversity ordering may partly reflect metric sensitivity.

The detection boundary $\alpha_c(T{=}10) \approx 0.49$ derives from a sub-linear signal model (Proposition~\ref{prop:phase-boundary}, $R^2{=}0.883$); predict-then-verify at $T{=}20$ reveals systematic conservative bias at boundary $\alpha$.
-The synchronous dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ persists across $T{=}10$, $15$, $20$, suggesting a structural regime distinct from \citet{gu2024cmr}.

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

We study lead-lag analysis pitfalls in iterative training collapse using Pythia-410M \cite{biderman2023pythia}, a 410M-parameter decoder-only language model.
Pythia provides a controlled setting: small enough for multi-seed experiments across thirteen contamination levels, yet large enough to exhibit meaningful generation-over-generation degradation.
Cross-architecture validation uses GPT-2-medium (345M parameters, also decoder-only), a second transformer family of similar scale; results are reported in \S\ref{sec:regime} and \S\ref{sec:discussion}.
Training data is drawn from WikiText-103 \cite{merity2017pointer}, using 5{,}000-sample subsets per generation.

Our protocol follows the replace paradigm of \citet{shumailov2024curse}, adapted for mixed synthetic-real training at $\alpha{<}1.0$.
Each generation $t$ proceeds in three steps: (1)~fine-tune the generation-$(t{-}1)$ model for 5{,}000 steps on a mixture of $\alpha$ fraction synthetic data and $(1{-}\alpha)$ fraction real data (AdamW optimizer, learning rate $5 \times 10^{-5}$, 500 warmup steps, weight decay $0.01$, batch size 4 for Pythia-410M, 32 for GPT-2-medium); (2)~generate 5{,}000 synthetic samples from the fine-tuned model (temperature $1.0$, top-$k{=}50$, max length 512 tokens); (3)~fully replace the synthetic pool.
We run $T{=}10$ generations across a 13-point $\alpha$ grid ($\{0.00, 0.05, 0.10, \ldots, 1.00\}$) with multi-seed replication (4 seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$; 3 at primary levels; 1--2 at probing points).

We track two \emph{canary metrics}---token entropy ($H(p_\theta | \text{context})$, 1{,}000 held-out samples) and ECE (15 bins)---and three \emph{downstream metrics}: distinct-1 and distinct-2~\cite{li2016diversity} and perplexity (evaluated on held-out real data).
Additional metrics (distinct-3, effective rank, Self-BLEU) appear in the Appendix.
Code and data will be released upon publication.

All hypothesis tests apply Benjamini--Hochberg (BH) FDR correction at $q{=}0.05$.
Permutation Granger causality tests use 5{,}000 permutations on first-differenced series \cite{shojaie2022granger}.
Cross-correlation analysis uses a maximum lag of 5 generations.
Raw metric drift from generation~0 to generation~10 is summarized in Appendix Table~\ref{tab:drift_summary}.


\subsection{Sharp Detection Onset}
\label{sec:regime}

Diversity collapse occurs at every contamination level: distinct-1 declines by $14.1\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$ (fine-tuning drift) and by $40.3{\pm}0.3\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.25$ (3-seed mean).
Despite this ubiquitous degradation, Granger-causal detectability is sharply regime-dependent.
The onset we report reflects PermG's statistical power curve crossing the detection floor at a critical contamination level, not the emergence of a new physical signal; this interpretation is confirmed by sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
Permutation Granger (PermG) tests find 0/8 canary$\to$downstream pairs FDR-significant from $\alpha{=}0.00$ through $\alpha{=}0.45$, then jump to 6/8 at $\alpha{=}0.50$ (2~fp32 seeds, consistent).
This transition is striking because cumulative synthetic fraction barely changes across the boundary: $C = 1{-}(1{-}\alpha)^{10}$ yields $99.75\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.45$ versus $99.90\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.50$, a difference of 0.15 percentage points, yet detection jumps from null to reliable.
Sigmoid regression on $T{=}10$ data alone yields $\alpha_c = 0.483 \pm 0.006$ ($R^2 = 0.969$); steepness $k$ is not statistically constrainable ($\mathrm{SE}(k) \approx k$), consistent with a step-function transition (Figure~\ref{fig:regime_map}).
This single-$T$ estimate is consistent with the joint model (\S\ref{sec:theory}), which yields $\alpha_c(T{=}10) = 0.487$ and predicts how the detection boundary shifts with observation length.
We cannot distinguish a sharp phase transition from the inflection point of a smooth power curve at current sample sizes ($T \leq 20$); the detection onset may simply reflect where signal strength crosses the PermG power threshold.
A Fisher exact test corroborates the categorical jump: 0/64 pairs FDR-significant at $\alpha \leq 0.45$ versus 18/32 at $\alpha \geq 0.50$ ($p = 3.45 \times 10^{-11}$); sub-threshold $p$-values at $\alpha{=}0.45$ ($p_{\mathrm{fdr}} = 0.059$--$0.091$) are consistent with proximity to the power boundary (\S\ref{sec:theory}).
A systematic robustness analysis (1{,}160 configurations) confirms specification-invariance of the onset.

First-differencing scopes the canary claim precisely.
Canary$\to$diversity pairs retain unanimous FDR significance after first-differencing ($24/24 \to 24/24$ across 4~seeds at $\alpha{=}1.0$, 6 pairs per seed), while canary$\to$perplexity collapses entirely ($F \approx 0$, $p = 0.99$): the apparent perplexity association is a shared-trend artifact.
All canary claims are therefore scoped to diversity metrics only.
This scoping reflects a genuine temporal structure difference, not selective power loss from differencing: $|r|$ retention is ${\geq}95\%$ for both channels, but canary$\to$diversity correlations peak at lagged offsets (81\% at lag${<}0$, median${=}-1$) while canary$\to$perplexity correlations are contemporaneous (50\% at lag${=}0$), producing $20$--$28{\times}$ lower Granger $F$ for perplexity (Appendix~\ref{app:channel_effect_size}; perplexity $n{=}8$, limited sample).
At $\alpha{=}1.0$, all 24 canary$\to$diversity pairs (6 per seed $\times$ 4~seeds; mauve excluded) reach FDR significance in the forward direction with 0/24 reverse; directional asymmetry is robust across all WikiText conditions.
Independent of the Granger test, the degradation cascade confirms temporal precedence: entropy onset at generation~1 precedes distinct-$n$ onset at generation~2 in 16/18 WikiText conditions (Kendall $\tau{=}0.337$; \S\ref{sec:cascade}, Appendix~\ref{app:moment_cascade}).
The canary mechanism also exhibits a blind spot: at $\alpha{=}0.10$, distinct-1 has already dropped by $39.6\%$, yet token entropy is indistinguishable from the null ($-5.3\%$ versus $-4.6{\pm}0.4\%$ at $\alpha{=}0.0$).
The gen-1 entropy deviation spans three orders of magnitude across the $\alpha$ range: $0.5\sigma$ at $\alpha{=}0.10$ to $60\sigma$ at $\alpha{=}0.75$ (relative to null variability), explaining why the blind zone persists despite increasing contamination.\footnote{Seed~43 at $\alpha{=}0.10$ shows 3/8 PermG FDR-significant pairs versus 0/8 for seed~42, consistent with stochastic variation at low signal rather than robust detection; no other below-threshold $\alpha$ level exhibits seed-dependent detection.}
Below $\alpha_c$ at $T{=}10$, diversity collapse proceeds without any detectable Granger-causal signal in the canary metrics.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

When language models train iteratively on their own output, the training distribution progressively loses its tail modes, a phenomenon termed model collapse~\cite{shumailov2024curse,alemohammad2024mad}.
Lexical diversity narrows, calibration deteriorates, and each generation inherits the systematic biases of its predecessors.
As machine-generated text becomes prevalent on the web, such feedback loops pose a growing risk to production training pipelines.
By the time standard quality metrics register degradation, the underlying distribution may have already shifted irreversibly.

This threat motivates a fundamental question: \emph{what does the detectability landscape of model collapse look like?}
At what contamination level does statistical detection become possible, how does this boundary depend on observation length and statistical method, and what structure does the landscape exhibit?
Iterative training produces short, noisy time series (often fewer than 15 points per generation sequence), where detection power drops sharply~\cite{boettiger2012limits}, and existing analyses leave these dependencies unresolved.
Our detection mechanism (Granger-causal temporal precedence) differs from critical-slowing-down indicators, as model collapse is a first-order transition~\cite{truong2026phase} (\S\ref{sec:related_work}).

We systematically map this landscape using Pythia-410M~\cite{biderman2023pythia} across thirteen contamination levels with multi-seed replication, applying five statistical methods from econometrics~\cite{granger1974spurious,toda1995statistical} to identical data.
The resulting map reveals structured terrain: blind zones where collapse proceeds undetected, a sharp onset where detection jumps from null to reliable within a 2-percentage-point interval, a synchronous dip where canary and downstream metrics collapse simultaneously, and a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ that follows a power law in observation length.
Cross-architecture validation across five families (345M--6.9B) confirms the landscape generalizes when entropy-diversity coupling is preserved.
Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causality~\cite{shojaie2022granger}; our canary claim is scoped to diversity metrics (distinct-$n$~\cite{li2016diversity}).

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Detectability landscape characterization} (\S\ref{sec:regime}--\ref{sec:intervention}).
    PermG reveals a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T) = \alpha_\infty + A \cdot T^{-1/(2\beta)}$ derived from a sub-linear signal model (Proposition~\ref{prop:phase-boundary}, $R^2{=}0.883$; theoretical $\gamma{=}2.408$ consistent with empirical $2.41$); below $\alpha_\infty{=}0.193$ no observation length suffices.
    Predict-then-verify at $T{=}20$ matches 3/5 predictions in saturated regimes, with systematic conservative bias at boundary $\alpha$ (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}); canary-triggered cessation reduces peak perplexity by 58\%.

    \item \textbf{Formal motivation for canary metric selection} (\S\ref{sec:cascade}).
    Under mode amplification, entropy Granger-precedes diversity (Proposition~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}), with a ${\geq}1$-generation lag (Proposition~\ref{prop:div_lag}), confirmed in 14/15 experiments ($\alpha \geq 0.30$; GPT-2-medium s43 bidirectional).

    \item \textbf{Method sensitivity as a primary finding} (\S\ref{sec:mmct}--\ref{sec:dose_response}).
    Five detection methods yield null-control FPR from 0\% to 92\%; the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 within a 2-percentage-point interval.
    The detectability landscape one observes depends critically on the statistical method used to probe it.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.9\textwidth]{figures/fig_dose_response.pdf}
\caption{The detectability landscape of iterative model collapse (Pythia-410M, fp32, PermG direction-checked). Four regimes emerge across 13 contamination levels: blind ($\alpha \leq 0.45$, 0/8), onset ($\alpha \approx 0.50$, 6/8), synchronous dip ($\alpha{=}0.60$, 0/8), and detection ($\alpha \geq 0.75$, 0--6/8). The detection boundary at $\alpha_c \approx 0.48$ follows a power law in $T$ (\S\ref{sec:theory}).}
\label{fig:regime_map}
\end{figure*}

\subsection{Extended Observation ($T{=}20$)}
\label{sec:t20}

$T{=}10$ ($\alpha{=}0.50$) serves as the single calibration point for $\alpha_c(T)$; $T{=}20$ provides a consistency check with greater statistical power.
Post-hoc power analysis (simulation under AR(1) DGP; Appendix~\ref{app:nonstationarity}) estimates PermG power at ${\sim}37\%$ for the diversity channel ($\hat{\beta}{\approx}0.59$) and ${\sim}25\%$ for perplexity ($\hat{\beta}{\approx}0.46$) at $T{=}10$; the 6/8 detection rate is consistent with moderate power rather than ceiling performance.
At $T{=}20$, estimated power increases to 55--65\% (diversity) and 35--45\% (perplexity), explaining the blind-zone shrinkage at $\alpha{=}0.45$ ($0/8{\to}5/8$).
Differenced perplexity channel power is ${\sim}14\%$ ($T{=}11$, $\hat{\beta}{=}0.46$), consistent with systematic non-detection and confirming this reflects low power rather than method failure.
We locked predictions at $T{=}10$ before running $T{=}20$ experiments (commit \texttt{bad72cc}), enabling predict-then-verify testing across five pre-registered $\alpha$ levels.
Excluding $\alpha{=}1.0$ (trivially $6/8{\to}6/8$), two of four predictions fall within CI ($\alpha \in \{0.50, 0.75\}$: $6/8{\to}6/8$); the boundary cases reveal systematic bias---$\alpha{=}0.45$ ($0/8$ predicted, $5/8$ observed) falsifies the ceiling model in favor of $\sqrt{T}$ power scaling, while $\alpha{=}0.60$ ($3/8$ predicted, $0/8$ observed) reflects the synchronous dip (Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}).\footnote{V1 (committed) used raw $p$-values; V2 (BH--FDR, 44\,min pre-analysis, not committed) predicted 0/8 for $\alpha{=}0.60$, matching observation.}
The synchronous dip at $\alpha{=}0.60$ persists at $T{=}20$ ($0/8$; FDR $p{=}0.064$).
Additionally, $\alpha{=}0.25$ (included as a negative control) unexpectedly yielded 3/8 detections; the joint model predicts $\alpha_c(T{=}20) = 0.248$ (Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c}), placing $\alpha{=}0.25$ just above the predicted boundary and $\alpha{=}0.45$ (5/8) well within the detection zone.
Transfer entropy provides independent validation: forward-dominant TE fraction increases monotonically with $\alpha$ (4/8 pairs at $\alpha{=}0.25$, 5/8 at $0.50$, 8/8 at $1.0$; mean net TE: $0.14 \to 1.59$), confirming the canary$\to$downstream directional structure without relying on the Granger framework (Appendix~\ref{app:te_mi}).

\subsection{Cross-Architecture Validation}
\label{sec:generalization}

We evaluate PermG across 15 model-seed combinations spanning five families (Pythia, GPT-2, OPT, Qwen, SmolLM3), scales from 345M to 6.9B, and two training domains (Table~\ref{tab:generalization}).
Detection succeeds when entropy--diversity coupling is preserved but reveals systematic failure modes when this coupling breaks down.

\paragraph{Detection conditions.}

Solving: $\alpha_c(T) = \alpha_\infty + (z^* \sigma / c)^{1/\beta} \cdot T^{-1/(2\beta)}$, giving the stated form with exponent $\gamma = 1/(2\beta)$.

\paragraph{Calibration and consistency.}
Fitting the theory model to 7 extrapolated points from Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c} ($T \in \{8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30\}$) yields $\alpha_\infty = 0.193$, $\beta = 0.208$, $A = 75.38$, $\gamma_{\mathrm{theory}} = 1/(2\beta) = 2.408$ (near-perfect by construction, since both models share the same functional form; the meaningful comparison is the joint sigmoid fit to raw data: $R^2 = 0.883$ vs.\ $0.711$ for a linear signal model).
The empirical power-law fit (Eq.~\ref{eq:alpha-c}) gives $\gamma = 2.41$, a discrepancy of $\Delta\gamma = 0.002$.
A linear signal model ($\beta = 1$, implying $\gamma = 0.5$) achieves $R^2 = 0.711$ and is rejected.

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

Lead-lag analysis in iterative training collapse is far more fragile than the current literature assumes.
Method choice alone inflates spurious-signal rates to at least 62.5\%, first-differencing exposes canary$\to$perplexity associations as entirely spurious, and regime dependence causes the same Granger test to shift from 24/24 to 0/8 significant pairs across contamination levels.
These pitfalls establish that single-method, single-regime analyses (the current default) cannot reliably distinguish genuine temporal precedence from statistical artifacts.

Our systematic five-method comparison through the Multi-Method Consensus Test (MMCT) identifies permutation Granger causality as the recommended detection method: it is the only one combining zero null-control FPR with high sensitivity, exhibiting a clean step-function dose-response from 0/8 (blind spot, $\alpha{\leq}0.45$) to 6/8 (onset, $\alpha{=}0.50$) with reliable detection at $\alpha{\geq}0.75$.
The other four methods each fail in characteristic ways: naive cross-correlation inflates FPR to 75\%, differenced cross-correlation cannot separate forward from reverse precedence, threshold onset is power-limited at $T{=}10$ under $3\sigma$ calibration, and Toda--Yamamoto Granger provides supplementary detection at reduced power (directional assignment under verification).

Applying permutation Granger, token entropy exhibits robust one-generation-ahead precedence over diversity collapse at $\alpha{=}1.0$ on WikiText-103 (24/24 forward, 0/24 reverse across 4~seeds, replicated on GPT-2-medium and OPT-1.3B), with cross-architecture validation confirming forward detection (${\geq}6/8$) in 13 of 15 model-seed combinations spanning five families (345M--6.9B), though one (GPT-2-medium s43) exhibits bidirectional significance.
Directional asymmetry is domain-dependent: consistent unidirectionality holds on WikiText across all regimes, while C4 exhibits near-symmetric bidirectional coupling at $\alpha{=}0.50$ (PermG reverse 7/8), though forward detection remains robust in both domains.
This finding is deliberately scoped to lexical diversity, not model collapse broadly, since the perplexity channel proved entirely spurious under differencing.

The methodological pitfalls we expose arise from generic properties of short, non-stationary time series.
Cross-architecture (five families, 345M--6.9B), cross-scale ($3.4\times$ within Pythia), and cross-domain (C4) validation confirms that both the pitfalls and the method recommendation are not specific to a single experimental configuration; evaluation on models at ${>}$7B parameters remains an open direction.
Limitations are detailed in \S\ref{sec:limitations}; future directions are discussed in \S\ref{sec:discussion}.
